facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Other legends state that the magnetic effect of the lodestone was so strong that it caused disturbance in the ships compasses... Portuguese sailors destroyed the temple and took away the lodestone.
facts.text: According to maritime folklore, Portuguese navigators dismantled the pinnacle magnet because its intense magnetic field allegedly disturbed ship compasses and caused vessels to run aground.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Vessels passing through the Konark sea were drawn to it, resulting in heavy damage... But there is no record of the existence of such a powerful load stone, whereas the shallow coast and shifting sands formed natural nautical hazards.
facts.text: While folklore attributes historical shipwrecks to magnetic attraction from the temple, maritime historians attribute these wrecks to treacherous coastal sandbars and monsoon shoals off the Konark shore.

facts.quote: The sundial has 8 major spokes that divide 24 hours into 8 equal parts (time gap between two major spokes is 3 hours or one prahara), with minor spokes dividing into 90 minutes.
facts.text: Each sundial wheel at Konark is engineered with eight major spokes that partition the daylight into three-hour spans known as praharas.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: While modern interpreters view the wheels as working sundials calibrated to solar movement, classical scholars emphasize their primary function as symbolic wheels of time representing the twelve months of the solar calendar.
facts.text: While local tourist guides demonstrate that shadows cast upon the wheel spokes calculate local solar time down to minutes, art historians argue the wheels served primarily as cosmological and calendar symbolism.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The theory of the lodestone's removal causing the collapse is uncorroborated; the fall was gradual, accelerated by sandy soil foundation weaknesses, weathering of stone, and loss of the finial.
facts.text: Historians dispute the exact cause of the main sanctum tower's collapse, debating whether it failed due to soft sandy subsoil subsidence, engineering flaws, or deliberate military desecration.

facts.text: The Samba Purana states that Krishna's son Samba endured twelve years of penance at Mitravana on the Chandrabhaga river to obtain Surya's blessing and cure his leprosy.

facts.text: The Madala Panji temple chronicle records that the general Kalapahad invaded Odisha in 1568 CE and displaced the crowning arch stone of the Konark temple complex.

sheet.summary: Popular folklore asserts that a 52-tonne lodestone magnet atop the Konark Sun Temple levitated the presiding deity and threw passing European ships off course by distorting their magnetic compasses until Portuguese sailors removed it. Archaeological surveys found no evidence of a giant magnet, discovering instead massive wrought-iron structural tie-beams and twenty-four monumental stone wheels engineered with eight major spokes that align with solar intervals. Historians and oceanographers disagree with the magnetic shipwreck theory, demonstrating that shallow sandbars and monsoonal coastal currents caused maritime groundings, while scholars debate whether the wheels were practical sundials or symbolic calendar art. What remains unknown is the definitive engineering failure that brought down the main 60-metre sanctum tower and the exact nature of the original crowning finial.
